findings.finding: Decision 25 has run start the waiter by the container's name and the scan count a build only by that waiter under a live driver; Behaviour 6 says another user's running build on docker or finch is now kept and that what clean removes is what is not running. The waiter is started only in mode build (watchExit/containerWait at container.go:117). mode shell returns into runHeld (container.go:110, 131), which starts no container wait; attach's `<rt> container exec -i -t warden-build-<id> ...` is not a waiter. So another user's live `warden shell` session (another HOME, lock not in keep_ids) has nothing the scan counts, and this user's warden clean tears it down on every runtime: finch case 6's failure, for the shell. On podman main kept it through conmon -n warden-build-<id>, which r4 drops (a regression there); on docker and finch main did not either (its shell exec named the 64-hex ID). guide/cli.md:408 now promises a running build is left alone while its warden-driver-container runs, even another user's. The design names no such gap; its run row and Decision 25 cover run in both modes.
findings.fix: In runHeld, once the held build container runs, start the same waiter by name under the driver (waitArgs, through watchExit or a bare containerWait whose result runHeld handles), with a test that a held run starts it. If Implement finds a waiter does not fit mode shell (e.g. what its exited means during a shell), back-to-design (FLOW-06) to name the gap instead. Either way keep cli.md:408 true to the result.

findings.finding: The change alters two security boundaries, as the design declares (security_boundary: host-env, and env-relay). (1) host-env: the code that builds the isolation is now chosen at run time by a lookup (PATH first, then beside warden, then linked), with no ownership or mode check (a16 as Jeff answered it). The one guard is that a config file may name a driver, not a file (driverlookup.go findByPath, sourceConfig). (2) env-relay: warden now makes the claim token and claims every driver's relay. The design's Security note covers both. In the code read, the guard is implemented as the note says: a relative or empty PATH entry is an error, on Windows only .exe is a candidate, and a non-executable file is skipped and listed. Carried from the previous reports, unchanged by 321017c, 274a988, the merge 78a4a6e and 4d3b760. MUST-review: this needs the human's sign-off at merge, not a fix.

deviations_judged.deviation: (1) The refusal prints twice: the relayed driver stderr line and warden's ERROR with its fix.
deviations_judged.judgment: Not a finding. The kit logs every error's message on the driver's stderr (driver/drivercmd/main.go:122, 281, since task 13; DRV-40) and warden relays it, then prints the error object, so every probe refusal on the branch prints twice (r3's --runtime nope too). Reproduced for --runtime, WARDEN_CTR_CLI, [driver.container] cli and doctor. r4 adds nothing new; the guide's examples show warden's lines only, as configuration.md:494 already did. See informational UX-04.

deviations_judged.deviation: (2) The ps parse splits at blanks; a runtime or driver path holding a space is not recognised and the build is left to keep_ids.
deviations_judged.judgment: Runtime half moot: the driver starts the waiter by the bare runtime name (exec.Command(name,...)) and paths are refused as the runtime setting (runtime_former.go), so the waiter's argv[0] is never a path. Driver half real: warden runs the driver as its full path (cmd/warden/drivercall.go:633, 769), so a driver path with a blank fails path.Base(parent.args[0]) (driver/container/clean.go:204), and another user's running build under it is removed. The design's 'base name of its first argument' is met only for paths without blanks; the design accepts the same degradation to keep_ids for BusyBox (driver-contract.md:5219) but does not name this one. Not counted; see informational FLOW-06.

deviations_judged.deviation: (3) Under the fault, the fake treats waiter.pid's presence as a live child, with no check that the process lives.
deviations_judged.judgment: Not a finding. The fault plays a driver that takes a process naming the build for a sign of life; in the Clean case the waiter really is alive when clean runs (it sleeps an hour and only stopRelay kills it), so a signal-0 check would answer the same. The self-test sees Clean fail under it, and stopStubRelays now also kills waiters (*.pid).

informational.note: The window before the waiter: even in mode build the waiter starts only after the relay container, the claim, the holder, the sidecar and the build container's start, pulls included, which can take minutes. Until then the scan finds nothing, and another user's starting build is not kept by it. On podman main kept it through the relay's and build's conmon; on docker and finch nothing did. Decision 25 drops the relay and conmon deliberately, so this follows from the approved wording, but Behaviour 6's 'what it removes is what is not running' overstates it. Name it in 'What Decision 25 relies on' (driver-contract.md:5219), or accept it explicitly. For Jeff, or Publish's design consolidation.

A driver path with a blank (deviation 2). Either Implement fixes the parse while it handles finding 4 (read each line as PID, PPID and the rest; the parent is the driver when the rest less a trailing ' run' has base name warden-driver-container; add a case under '/opt/my tools/'), or the design names the limit beside BusyBox at consolidation. Jeff's call. Not counted, because its effect falls back to keep_ids, as the accepted degradations do.

Every fixable probe or command error from a driver binary prints its message twice: the driver's log line and warden's ERROR. If Jeff wants one line, warden could leave out a relayed last line equal to the error's message, or the kit could stop logging errors it also returns. Either is contract-wide, and not on main, so not a FLOW-09 follow-up.

teardown now calls stopRelay(dir) after relay.Process.Kill(), and stopRelay kills relay.pid's PID again. By then the goroutine's relay.Wait() may have reaped the relay, and if the PID was reused an unrelated process gets the signal. The window is microseconds and this is a test double. Killing only waiter.pid in teardown closes it.
